PORT MORESBY, National Superannuation Fund Limited (Nasfund) has been delivering its Superannuation (Supa) Education Sessions in schools across PNG since 2024 as part of its commitment to preparing young Papua New Guineans for their future financial journey.

The program is a superannuation education and awareness initiative designed to educate students to understand superannuation, retirement savings and personal financial planning.

The initiative equips participants with essential superannuation education, including how superannuation works, understanding the role of Nasfund, the importance of starting to save early, strategies for growing retirement savings and the value of making informed financial decisions throughout life.

As part of this ongoing initiative, Nasfund Member Experience Manager, Melisha Sindiwan, conducted three Supa Education sessions over the past two weeks at Port Moresby Grammar School, providing Grade 12 students with a practical introduction to superannuation and long-term financial planning.

The sessions were very engaging and focused on building awareness around superannuation education, encouraging students to begin thinking about their financial planning well before they enter the workforce. Students were introduced to the basics of superannuation, the role it plays in securing finances and retirement savings, and the benefits of establishing savings habits.

This marks the third consecutive year that Nasfund has partnered with Port Moresby Grammar School to deliver the Supa Education program under school enrichment program for grade 12s, reinforcing the Fund's commitment to investing in financial literacy and empowering future generations with the knowledge needed to make sound financial decisions.

Speaking on the importance of the program, Port Moresby Grammar School Director Curriculum for Senior School, Brenda Kekeao, said the Supa Education sessions align closely with the school's future financial planning module.

"For this module, we actually looked at other organisations, but the school chose Nasfund because of the long-standing relationship the school has with the company," Ms Kekeao said.

"From these sessions, we hope this will help educate students about their future financial planning."

Port Moresby: In Papua New Guinea, 44 out of every 100 women diagnosed with breast cancer succumb to the disease, according to Pacific International Hospital (PIH) Consultant Oncologist Dr. Michael Shawel Lemma.

Dr. Lemma shared the statistics during a breast cancer awareness session at Nasfund’s headquarters, held as part of the fund’s support for Pinktober. He said outcomes depend heavily on early detection and completing the recommended treatment.

He said breast cancer accounts for more than 20% of cancer cases treated at PIH, underscoring the need for greater awareness of its signs and symptoms and the importance of early detection.

“When breast cancer is diagnosed while it is confined to the breast, the five-year survival rate is 99%. If it has spread to the lymph nodes, the rate is 87%,” Dr Lemma said.

Dr Lemma said many women in PNG seek medical attention only after developing large lumps or open wounds, when treatment is more difficult and the likelihood of a cure is lower.

Other barriers include limited access to radiotherapy and diagnostic services, as well as distance, cost, fear, and cultural beliefs.

Nasfund staff and management attended the session at the Port Moresby headquarters, while teams from centers outside Port Moresby joined online.

This year’s Pinktober theme is “Every story is unique, every journey matters”.

Nasfund General Manager Talent and Culture Alex Rogea, speaking on behalf of Chief Executive Officer Rajeev Sharma, thanked the PIH team and acknowledged the participation of both female and male employees.

Central Province: In our society, service delivery can be very difficult to reach some of the most remote parts of the country. With Nasfund's Member Service Booths, we can reach some members and this week we attended to more than 100 members of the Seventh Day Adventist (SDA) Pastors Central Papua Conference at Mt Diamond in Central.

Nasfund team attending to participants of the SDA Pastors Central Papua Conference at Mt Diamond in Central last week.

Speaking on behalf of the members, Tubuseria Village, SDA Church Pastor Jacob Mavo said having the Nasfund Service Booth team stationed at the conference venue was a very "good idea".

"From this engagement, pastors have now realized that we do not utilize well some of the services you provide, especially the voluntary contributions platform, " Mavo said.

"Our church has been really great especially in building our retirement savings and we are very blessed."

Mavo said other products like the housing advance product should also be utilized because pastors housing has been a very big issue within the church.

He thanked Nasfund for bringing their essential services like helping members to log in to their online platforms, issuance of Eda Supa forms, providing member detail update forms and attending to general enquiries.

9-mile Ridge in Port Moresby SDA church pastor Samuel James said Nasfund's mobile service booth at the conference this week was a great way to serve their members.

"We have pastors who contribute with Nasfund but have come from very inland parts of Central but they were given the service here and at their doorstep," he said,

Nasfund Chief Executive Officer, Rajeev Sharma, attended the Pacific Islands Investment Forum (PIIF) Investment Conference held in Denarau, Fiji, from 24 to 26 August 2026, representing Nasfund as a member of PIIF while also participating in his capacity as President of the Association of Superannuation Funds of Papua New Guinea (ASFPNG) and Treasurer of PIIF.

Caption: Nasfund CEO Rajeev Sharma and members of the Pacific Islands Investment Forum (PIIF) at the PIIF Investment Conference in Denarau, Fiji. Picture Courtesy of PIIF Communications Team

The three-day conference brought together superannuation funds, investment professionals, development partners, and regional stakeholders to advance discussions on sustainable investment opportunities across the Pacific.

Organised in partnership with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (UNSDG) initiative, the conference focused on strengthening the PIIF Investment Platform, supporting the mobilisation of Pacific capital, developing investment-ready projects, enhancing governance frameworks, and building investment capacity across member funds.

The conference programme featured presentations and knowledge-sharing sessions from leading institutional investors, including representatives from the New Zealand Super Fund and the Australian Retirement Trust, reflecting the growing engagement between Pacific investment funds and major regional financial institutions.

PIIF Secretariat Executive Director, Damien Beddoes, said the conference provided an important platform for collaboration among member funds and partners.

"The conference creates opportunities for meaningful engagement through breakout sessions and networking, allowing members and partners to progress discussions on strategic investments, partnerships, governance, and regional development initiatives," Mr Beddoes said.

He added that the event would provide key decision-makers with greater insight into the Pacific Investment Platform, its benefits for member funds, emerging investment opportunities, and practical ways to leverage collective resources for regional growth.

Mr Sharma said his participation at the conference reflected Nasfund's continued commitment to contributing to discussions on regional economic development and long-term investment opportunities that benefit members.
